runtime.execution: Immutable agent command decisions; OTP GenServer signal routing, supervised directives/actions and storage adapters.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns agent runtime/supervisors/ephemeral instance control state; user actions consume external programs/services. AI belongs to companion integration.

summary: Pluggable strategies, explicit state and runtime-owned effects, with append-only interaction thread/checkpoint support.

inspection.scope: command normalization/hooks, signal router/call/cast, directive effect execution, runtime store, thread/persistence/file adapter and test assertions
inspection.limits: Jido.Action/Jido.Signal dependency implementations are not in this reference; no arbitrary remote effect settlement or BEAM hot code upgrade traced.

actions.name: Agent.cmd
actions.input: agent struct, action/instruction list and context/options
actions.output: new agent plus runtime directive list or validation error
actions.lifecycle: functional strategy decision with before/after hooks; action execution may be effectful

actions.name: AgentServer.call / cast
actions.input: PID/logical server ID, typed Signal, call timeout
actions.output: updated agent/error or immediate enqueue acknowledgment
actions.lifecycle: serialized actor handling; cast is not completion receipt

actions.name: Directive.Emit / RunInstruction
actions.output: dispatch task or normalized result/effects re-enter strategy
actions.lifecycle: supervised external dispatch can be fire-and-forget; RunInstruction feeds command
actions.authority: authored directive handlers and propagated context

actions.name: Directive.Spawn / Schedule
actions.output: child PID/runtime effect or timer-delivered signal
actions.lifecycle: supervised child; process-local timer; explicit hard stop can orphan work

actions.name: Persist.hibernate / thaw
actions.input: storage adapter, agent module/key and state
actions.output: checkpoint or reconstructed agent/error with exact thread revision
actions.lifecycle: journal flush precedes checkpoint; thaw logical state, no live task migration

actions.name: Thread.append / storage append_thread
actions.output: new revision and ordered entries or conflict
actions.lifecycle: append authored facts; projection separate; storage adapter durability varies
actions.authority: application decides what original events to append

actions.name: RuntimeStore.get/fetch/put/delete
actions.lifecycle: survives API process but not owning instance restart
actions.authority: Jido instance control plane, not external service authority

filesystem.detail: Owned file adapter stores checkpoints/journals; user-supplied action modules can perform other I/O, not a built-in coding-agent file tool catalog.

processes.detail: BEAM actor/task spawn and delayed signal primitives; OS process runner belongs to authored actions/dependencies, not core catalog.

code_actions.detail: Validated authored action modules execute with state/context and feed result/effects into strategy; core is not a Python-code model action.

persistent_kernel.detail: Long-lived GenServer/state can host application computation; no independent shared interpreter kernel supplied by actor lifetime.

standing_database.detail: Storage adapters retain checkpoints/threads; RuntimeStore is explicitly ephemeral instance-owned ETS, not a durable shared standing application DB.

workflow_programming.detail: Strategies, normalized instructions, hooks, custom directive protocols, signal routing and supervised effects form actual programmable orchestration.

multi_model.detail: Core explicitly has no provider integration; Jido.AI companion is separately studied.

live_collaboration.detail: Signal-addressed actors/parent-child spawn and dispatch compose peers; not an IRC/model collaboration UI without AI integration.

concurrent_work.detail: Supervised actor/task/dispatch processes can run concurrently; individual GenServer signal processing serial.

steering_interrupt.detail: Signals enqueue state changes but hard stop can orphan async work/drop directives; no universal effect-settled pause/refit barrier.

turn_redefinition.detail: Strategy.cmd and before/after hooks redefine application decision programs; routes initialized from modules, not automatically model-authored/hot core turns.

compaction.detail: Append-only interaction Thread versus separate context projection is useful basis; summarizer/compaction policy outside core.

context_repair.detail: Original thread and explicit restore with rev check supply repair/reprojection inputs; no model-native repair action in core.

original_audit.detail: Appended authored interaction entries preserved independently from context; not all action/provider/OS I/O automatically captured, with queue overflow/hard-stop gaps.

audit_query.detail: Thread entries/checkpoint retrieval and revision pointers are inspectable storage primitives, not whole-machine audit database/query tools.

hot_change.detail: No wired code_change/upgrade/refit mechanism established in command/router/persist paths; BEAM capability alone is not evidence.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Logical checkpoint/thread/scheduler manifests reconstruct state and reject mismatch; process timers/tasks/ETS do not survive as active work. No outpost protocol.

remote_services.detail: Custom action and signal-dispatch integrations consume external services; shared service governance is not implied by agent supervision.

self_improvement.detail: Application-owned strategies/actions/protocols make experiment machinery implementable, but no model-governed automatic improvement loop supplied.

complaints.detail: Error directives/queue-overflow and traced signals support diagnostics; full snapshot complaint tracking would need composition.

authority.detail: Runtime invokes authored module/route/plugin and action context; dependency/remote credentials and approval policy supplied by application.

evaluation.detail: Reusable storage contract asserts exact roundtrip/overwrite/delete/missing results; plugin integration asserts routing effects. No live-provider or crash-durability test execution here.

time_order.detail: Thread revision, expected-rev append and checkpoint pointer check; GenServer signal order distinct from fire-and-forget task/timer completion.

evidence.claim: Command hooks normalize instructions with current state/signal, delegate strategy.cmd and after-command; commands may perform effectful actions.
Strategy/agent/plugin routes have explicit priority and target action/module/strategy command; router built from those sources.
call/cast resolve agent server reference; GenServer call waits for signal result while cast enqueues asynchronously.
Emit propagates trace context and dispatches self or supervised external dispatch task; no durable acknowledgment ledger shown.
RunInstruction executes action then feeds normalized result/effects back into command, updating state and enqueuing directives; queue overflow logs and drops.
Spawn starts supervised child; Schedule uses Process.send_after for attributed delayed signal, process-local timer not durable by itself.
Custom directive protocol is extension surface; documented hard stop drops pending effects and can orphan async work; completion should be state, not exit.
RuntimeStore ETS is instance-owned ephemeral coordination; survives its API process restart but not instance stop/restart.
Canonical Thread is provider-agnostic append-only entries, monotonic rev; model context is projected rather than destructively stored there.
Hibernate flushes thread journal then creates/stores checkpoint; separate operations, not atomic external-effect settlement.
Checkpoint strips embedded runtime thread and stores id/rev pointer plus state/scheduler manifest.
Thaw validates/migrates checkpoint, reconstructs agent/thread/manifest and checks state budget; thread rev mismatch/missing journal rejected.
File checkpoint term serialization writes temp then rename; no fsync or multiprocess checkpoint CAS established here.
Thread append validates expected revision, appends encoded entries then writes metadata; runtime effect occurs outside this storage sequence.
Real GenServer/plugin tests assert override suppresses normal increment and rejection yields error, not merely no crash.

tests.oracle: Exact missing/roundtrip/overwrite/arbitrary-term/delete assertions shared across adapters; does not establish power-loss/fsync/thread semantics.
GenServer test asserts overridden action state and zero normal increment; error leaves state unchanged.

strengths: Separates logical strategy, effectful actions and runtime effect directives without falsely declaring all actions pure.
Original interaction thread can be projected independently; checkpoint binds its exact revision.
Direct actor/plugin and storage contract oracles are useful patterns.
limits: Core is AI-optional and no provider/kernel agent loop.
Ephemeral ETS/timers and fire-and-forget dispatch are not durable replay/settlement.
No traced BEAM hot upgrade makes language-level hot code support an Arconaut feature.
arconaut_questions: Which effect directives deserve acknowledgment handles versus deliberate fire-and-forget?
How should original events be automatically captured beyond application-chosen Thread entries?
What explicit effect barrier is needed before checkpoint/recompile?
